finding.text: Scoping uses `?scope=2026-10` (AISessionsPage.js:37, set_scope) instead of the asked `/2026/10/` routes. compact-layout.md explains why: those paths already belong to StoreFolder. It is a sound, documented call, and each filter is still a URL.

The left rail (`nav_view`, AISessionsPage.js:~122) is a new hand-built link list, though the brief said "reuse, never a new one". The doc says no vertical nav fit. The active item is hard-coded to index 0, and the other entries leave the page, so the rail disappears when you click them. Sub-views are not really in-page routes yet.
The brief asked for a docs view and health/cost views as rail entries. Only Priorities, Readme and the dashboard versions are there.

The rail has no "All sessions" crumb, though the render_scope comment mentions one. The year is the top level, so there is no way back to an unscoped list. Month is the default and the arrows step the level.

The first row is at y=267 of 1000 at 1200, about 27%, near the ~25% target. The diff holds no 400 / 1920 / 3440 shots or first-row/rows-visible numbers for those widths. I could not check the four widths or the `:has(.sessions-page)` footer hide, whose class name was not verified in the diff.
The diff includes generated churn in `sessions/files.jsonl` ("gone" entries for json files and screenshots/). It is unrelated to the layout work and just noise.

`set_scope` hides the date inputs but keeps them in sync, so the "hand edits don't update the breadcrumb" caveat is moot. Hiding them with `display:none` (sessions.css util layer) leaves no manual range at all, and the brief did not ask for that.

None of the four shot pages is the Sessions grid. They are a day page, two session detail pages and an ai2 card, so the changed status rail (`.sessions-status` in `sessions.css`) is not visible in any shot. Requirements 2, 3 and 4 cannot be confirmed from these shots, and the first-row y, footer height and left padding are not measured.

The diff is only a CSS tweak to `.sessions-status`, plus `files.jsonl` / `page.jsonl` noise. It adds no scope breadcrumb, no left rail and no routes. If those landed earlier in `michael/dev`, this review cannot see them. Re-shoot `/framework/ai/sessions/` and `/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/`, then review again.
The diff hides the second `.sessions-counts` (the OpenRouter dollars) with `display: none`. That is an information loss and the rail now has no way to show it.
Widths given: 400, 1200, 1920 and 3440. Every page has one tab row at 1200 and above, 2 at 400. No overflow_x.

The status rail is not one line. At 1200 it takes four lines: the counts line, the OpenRouter line, the meters with "5h session" and "weekly" wrapped, and the open-tasks chip alone on a last line (shots/sessions/1200.png, bottom band). Ask 2 says "one line, small text".

At 400 the rail is clipped: the counts text runs off the right edge ("2026-10…", the "weekly — Fable" meter is cut off) and it sits over the last visible rows (shots/sessions/400.png, bottom band). The `nowrap` on `.ai-meter` is the likely cause.

The first row is not in the top ~25% at 1200. "Ultracode" sits at y≈290 of 900 (~32%), under the toolbar, the search/filter row and a wrapped two-row routine-chip row (shots/sessions/1200.png, bands 1–2). The diff changes none of this, so the header compaction in ask 2 is unmet or landed elsewhere.

The shots that review.mjs auto-picked are not the Sessions page (a day page, two session detail pages and an ai2 card), and `shots/sessions/` has no layout.json. Tab rows, wraps and band shares cannot be measured for the changed page. Sizing and spacing answers below come from the PNGs only. The task's before/after numbers (first-row y, footer height, left padding) are not in the folder.

`.sessions-counts + .sessions-counts { display: none }` hides the OpenRouter dollars. The screenshot shows this rule is not applied, because the line is still visible at 1200, so the rule and the picture disagree.

The diff is one CSS block plus `files.jsonl` / `page.jsonl` noise. The rail, scope breadcrumb and routes seen in the shots came from earlier commits, so this diff cannot be judged against asks 3 and 4.
Widths given: 400, 1200, 1920 and 3440 (1920 and 3440 were not opened).

Ask 2 "first row in the top ~25% at 1200" is not met — shots/sessions/1200.png: first row title at y≈370 of 900 (≈41%); the filter chips (routine and role, two rows each) take the band between y 130 and 340. At 1920 the first row is at y≈387 of 1080 (≈36%).

The status rail is still two lines at 1200 and six lines at 400 (shots/sessions/1200.png bottom, 400.png bottom ≈ 150 px). The ask was one line of small text and icons; the "show 30 more days" button and the "1 open task on this page" chip are still plain buttons, not icon chips. Only 1920 comes close to one line.

Ask 3 day scoping is not visible — the breadcrumb reads "2026 / October" with ‹ › and "today"; there is no day level, so /2026/10/13/ cannot be reached from it (shots/sessions/1200.png, band under the title).
At 1920 the Role cell clips the MASTERMIND tag under the SERVEX tag on the first row (shots/sessions/1920.png, row 1, Role/Source columns).

The page left a status-rail CSS-only diff; there is no layout.json for shots/sessions, so tab_rows, bands and left padding were judged from the shots. The diff is mostly files.jsonl churn (unrelated gone/added lines); only sessions.css matters.
The status rail's fixed `.ai-gauge` and `white-space: nowrap` meters make the 400 rail tall; let them stack as one chip per meter or hide the gauges below ~600px.
